StudyFlow — Research and Technical DocumentationOverview
The Problem

Long hours, little retained

  • Students default to passive rereading, cramming and marathon sessions — habits poorly matched to how memory works.
  • Decades of cognitive research point the other way: retrieval practice, spacing, interleaving and focused work with real breaks.
  • The techniques are known — but they are hard to organise and sustain with paper timetables and willpower alone.
  • StudyFlow's premise: turn the evidence into a workspace students actually use every day.
StudyFlow — Research and Technical DocumentationSlide 2
The Product

One connected study workspace

  • A Pomodoro-style Focus Desk with tasks, streaks and sessions.
  • A guided library of study techniques with a personal fit assessment.
  • A book library with an in-browser EPUB reader and companion prompts.
  • Ambient sound studios for focused work.
  • A social layer: groups, messaging, voice/video calls, expiring statuses.
  • A reward economy: coins, achievements and a store.

Learning Science

A session cycle designed from the evidence

Focus → short break → repeat → long break
  • Work in focused intervals separated by restorative breaks.
  • Breaks and limits counter attention residue from task switching.
  • The desk nudges the cycle; the student stays in control.

Feature — Motivation

Coins, achievements and a store

The reward store
  • Focus sessions and streaks earn coins.
  • Achievements mark real milestones, not busywork.
  • The store turns consistency into visible progress.
  • Gamification follows the research on careful extrinsic rewards — supporting, not replacing, intrinsic motivation.
StudyFlow — Research and Technical DocumentationSlide 8
Under the Hood

A disciplined vanilla-JS architecture

  • Single static shell; routes lazy-load as ES-module chunks.
  • Main bundle ≈ 288 kB; everything else fetched on demand.
  • A service worker precaches the shell — the app works fully offline.
StudyFlow — Research and Technical DocumentationSlide 9
Under the Hood

Supabase: PostgreSQL, auth and enforced privacy

Entity map (simplified)
  • 41 PostgreSQL tables across 24 migrations.
  • 136 Row Level Security policies — privacy enforced by the database, not the client.
  • Auth, Storage and Realtime channels from one managed platform.
  • No self-hosted servers; no secrets in the client.
StudyFlow — Research and Technical DocumentationSlide 10
Under the Hood

Real-time presence, statuses and calls

JWT sessions through Supabase Auth
WebRTC peer-to-peer voice & video, optional TURN
  • Expiring status updates (24-hour lifetime, server-enforced).

Closing

What is real, and what comes next

  • Built and verified: the full platform documented feature-by-feature against the codebase.
  • Honest limits: no experimental evaluation of learning outcomes yet; React/Tailwind scaffolding unused.
  • Next: a controlled study of StudyFlow's effect on retention, plus social and content expansion.
